articles.title: Property Domain Onboarding: Idempotent SPF, DKIM, DMARC TXT Publication Before Cutover
articles.excerpt: Gate property-manager onboarding on a recorded sending-domain verification result after an idempotent TXT publication job. Keep propagation waiting outside the cutover decision: the time at which a DN…
articles.body: Gate property-manager onboarding on a recorded sending-domain verification result after an idempotent TXT publication job. Keep propagation waiting outside the cutover decision: the time at which a DNS write is accepted is a poor substitute for evidence that the sending service recognizes the domain. TL;DR: Publish the configured SPF, DKIM, and DMARC TXT records in one job keyed by domain, safely repeat the upserts after partial completion, then request sending-domain verification and retain its result. Complete onboarding only when that result satisfies the application's explicit readiness policy. A property management platform needs this distinction when a manager connects a domain for resident correspondence. “The request succeeded” is an integration observation.

articles.title: 6 Object Storage Services for Browser File Uploads: Node.js Presigned URL Retention
articles.excerpt: Property managers usually need two different things from one upload: a browser should deliver a training artifact without proxying the bytes through the app, and the organization should be able to exp…
articles.body: Property managers usually need two different things from one upload: a browser should deliver a training artifact without proxying the bytes through the app, and the organization should be able to explain how long that artifact remains. Those goals pull in different directions. The practical choice is a private object store with presigned delivery and a retention policy owned by your application, not a public bucket with a clever URL. Short URLs do not fix retention. Suppose a regional manager uploads a revised fire-safety recording for property 204.

articles.title: Jest, Vitest, or node:test? Fixing "Cannot use import statement outside a module" by Choosing the Right Runner
articles.excerpt: If Jest just failed with SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module, your project is ESM and Jest is still running your files through a CommonJS pipeline. For a new TypeScript/ESM proje…
articles.body: If Jest just failed with SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module , your project is ESM and Jest is still running your files through a CommonJS pipeline. For a new TypeScript/ESM project, Vitest is the lowest-friction fix; node:test is enough if you have no browser code and few mocks; keep Jest if you have a large existing suite that already works. Below is why the error happens, the dead ends, and a decision table. Why does Jest say "Cannot use import statement outside a module"? The full symptom usually looks like this: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module 1 | import { slugify } from "./slugify.js"; | ^^^^^^ Jest runs each test file inside a sandboxed VM and, by default, expects CommonJS.

articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified.
